subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal complete-or-clear-fail fix, or a documented decision that current coarse scopes are the intended core boundary?
rationale: The issue is valid enough to keep open, but choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and sensitive data, and an open linked PR already owns the implementation discussion.

options.title: Narrow and review native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

options.title: Ship minimal reliability first
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress or size guidance, while deferring custom exclusion policy to the broader native-exclude tracker.

options.title: Defer core scope expansion
options.body: Document current backup limits and point users to plugin/workaround options only if maintainers explicitly decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.
